summary: Stage 5 of the rewrite is sound and attacks a real cost, and it is not moot under master, which still runs the scalar Python dequant at T>4096. But the expected magnitude is about 2-3x too optimistic, and with no GPU to test the hand-written PTX before a scored submit, prepare() must fall back to today's dequant if the packed variant fails to compile or fails _check_expert_gemms.
justification: Mechanism: plausible. On master the T>4096 path (_moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel, BLOCK_T 256/BLOCK_W 128/BLOCK_K 128, 8 warps, 2 stages) takes 8149-8873 us per first_turn shape (37-58% of the shape), about 5x the 1.67 ms w13+w2 math floor. It dequantizes every [128,128] weight tile once per 256-token tile with scalar int32 chains: load as int32, two and/shift/or chains, a truncate, a bitcast and a bf16 mul. The bit placement checks out. (t<<6)&0x01C001C0 | (t<<12)&0x80008000 and (t<<2)&0x01C001C0 | (t<<8)&0x80008000 reproduce today's ((b&7)<<6)|((b&8)<<12) and ((b&0x70)<<2)|((b&0x80)<<8) in each 16-bit half, with no cross-half leakage after masking, and the product stays exact (<= 6 significant bits). Because the op is elementwise and is_pure, correctness does not depend on how Triton groups the 4 packed elements, as long as output j maps to input byte j. Weakest link: magnitude. (1) An ALU count bounds the gain. Dequantized elements ~ 8.25e11 MAC / 256 ~ 3.2e9 (plus padding) x ~11 instructions ~ 3.5e10 lane-ops, against ~3.3e13 lane-ops/s on 132 SMs: about 1 ms of the 8.1-8.9 ms in total, not 3 ms. (2) Measured evidence agrees. Stage 3 halved the redundant dequants (BLOCK_T 128 to 256) and took w13+w2 only from 9.1-10.0 to 8.0-8.7 ms (~1.1-1.3 ms), so dequant at BLOCK_T 256 is about 1.1-1.3 ms. A ~70% cut saves ~0.7-0.9 ms. The realistic outcome is w13+w2 ~7.3-8.0 ms (5-11% on the kernel, ~4-6% on first_turn shapes, about +2-3% on the headline since first_turn is one of three loads), not 5-6 ms. Milestone 2 (beat the incumbent kernels) is likely, the stated 'under 7.0 ms' is unlikely, and milestone 3 (1.5x floor, ~2.5 ms) is out of reach in this stage. The other ~6 ms of the 5x gap is untouched: the sb_lo/sb_hi permute/reshape/broadcast (likely its own convert_layout), the register-LHS operand conversion, 2-stage pipelining at 256x128 and per-expert padding (~512 rows per expert padded to 256-row tiles). The ttgir convert_layout/local_alloc diagnostic that targets this is the most valuable part of the run. (3) The claim that the bf16 mul is fp32 mul plus two converts is unverified on this Triton; on sm_90 it may already emit native bf16 mul that ptxas pairs into HMUL2, which would shrink the win further. (4) Packing risk: if the code tile's layout does not give each thread 4 contiguous bytes (wgmma register-A layouts hold 2-element k pairs), Triton assembles each 32-bit register with extra byte inserts or prmts, and the asm result may need a blocked-to-dot-operand convert that today's elementwise chain avoided by hoisting. Either can erase the gain, and the per-variant n_regs/ttgir counts are what tell. Expected directions are consistent with TASK.md: first_turn faster, and turn_* structurally neutral because the stage-4 gate routes T<=4096 to Marlin and that code is byte-identical.
confounders: experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 (stage 3): sets BLOCK_T 256, which already halved the per-token-tile dequant count. The gain from cheaper dequant is smallest at this tile and would be about 2x larger at BLOCK_T 128. This sizes the effect but does not confound its attribution (the change applies at the same config), so no A/B is needed. Note it when sizing stage 6 (turn_4, BLOCK_T 128), where packed dequant should matter relatively more.

experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn (stage 4): the T<=4096 Marlin gate means only the first_turn shapes run the changed kernel. turn_1 and turn_4 are byte-identical code, so any movement there is run drift (LESSONS: 1.5-2.5% per shape). _check_expert_gemms still compiles and checks the BLOCK_T 64/128 configs in prepare(), so a packed-asm bug in those configs fails the run even though they are never timed.
sglang-pipeline-parity: everything around the experts. It does not interact with the dequant path.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage judged on _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel's own time per first_turn shape in top_kernels. Triton kernel times reproduce within ~1%, so a 0.5-1 ms move on 8.1-8.9 ms is readable from one run without a headline A/B. A PACKED_DEQUANT=False control would be byte-identical in behavior to master, which is already measured (fb1e52d2119d4175), so it adds nothing. Reverting stage 3 or 4 would only re-measure known configs. The follow-up is stage 6 (experts-triton-packed-dequant-turn4), informed by this run's ttgir counts.
rules_flags: None blocking. Inline PTX is allowed (another problem's submission already uses tl.inline_asm_elementwise). There is no BF16 weight copy, the dequant stays in registers per the user's ruling, the product is exact in BF16, and there is no host sync or input-derived caching.

If the subnormal fallback is needed (re-placing codes at a larger power of two), keep SCALE_BIAS * 448 within the bf16 range and the product exact. Re-check that the -0.0 addend in fma.rn.bf16x2 preserves signed zeros (it does with -0.0, not +0.0).
The added ttgir/compile diagnostics must stay in prepare(). Never print or read compiled metadata inside kernel_fn.
open_questions: Scored-submit safety, which I recommend as a condition of dispatch. With no GPU here the PTX (prmt selectors, packing order, tuple return) cannot be tested before the run, and any compile error or _check_expert_gemms mismatch aborts prepare() and burns the scored submit. Make PACKED (or PACKED_DEQUANT) a tl.constexpr kernel argument, not a module global: Triton rejects or ignores a global changed after compile. In prepare(), try the packed variant for every EXPERT_CONFIGS entry under try/except around compile plus _check_expert_gemms. On failure, print the exception and the mismatch summary to the log and set state['packed']=False so every variant runs today's dequant. _experts_triton then passes state's flag. This is a small, deliberate deviation from 'byte-identical _experts_*'. kernel_fn branches only on prepare-time state (fine under the rules), and the run then measures master's kernel instead of failing.

Does Triton on this image hoist the dot-operand convert_layout above today's elementwise dequant chain, so the dequant runs directly in the wgmma register-A layout? If it does, and it refuses to hoist above inline_asm with pack=4, the packed version adds a blocked-to-dot-operand convert, possibly through shared memory, and could be slower despite fewer ALU ops. Print the convert_layout/local_alloc counts for both PACKED=False and PACKED=True (compile both in prepare) so the log answers this directly.
Is the bf16 multiply already native HMUL2.BF16 on sm_90 in this Triton version? If yes, the per-element saving is ~6-8 instructions, not 7-9, and the win is near the low end of ~0.5-0.9 ms.

Should the sb_lo/sb_hi permute/reshape/broadcast also move into the asm? Each register could take the 8 compact scales per row and select by group index. It is left byte-identical here and may be a comparable cost. The ttgir counts should show whether it is a convert_layout of its own.
